title: The goal is better patient identification
sub: Find more patients likely to initiate advanced therapy at the same targeting capacity.
items: The 49-feature LightGBM supports HCP targeting. Reported historical lift: 4.59. Its population and evaluation differ; this is not a matched development comparison.
Monthly medical histories, richer feature representations and controlled model comparisons. Business rules stay unchanged.
More positive patients captured for the same outreach capacity. Current experiments measure patient-date snapshots; unique-patient reporting is the next bridge to targeting.
note: Historical production lift belongs to its original evaluation. A matched production comparison is deferred.

sub: Progress includes stronger inputs and evaluation discipline as well as model development.

title: A common data foundation supports fair comparisons
sub: The expanded cohort contains 449,199 snapshots from 25,925 patients.
takeaway: All current model comparisons use the same validation rows. A snapshot is one patient at one date.
note: Patient-separated splits. Current development does not score TEST. Snapshot window: February 2022 to January 2026.

title: Medical histories enrich the original tabular approach
sub: The current phase combines twelve monthly history windows with one AutoML summary anchor.
items: Diagnosis, procedure and prescription activity describe what happened and how frequently.
Monthly text representations of medical codes add information about the types of recorded activity. These are not clinical notes.
Static AutoML features provide context. Sleep-study and sleep-wake timing features test whether recency adds predictive value.
note: A full twelve-anchor historical AutoML panel remains a separate experiment.

title: NLP fusion leads the current top-10% ranking
sub: 2.954 versus 2.533: +16.6%, or 48 additional positive snapshots at the same 10% capacity.
takeaway: Paired lift interval: +0.009 to +0.802. NLP leads at 10%; static fusion leads slightly at 20% and 30%.
note: Development validation. Added information differs across models. Lift is selected positive rate divided by overall positive rate.

title: Timing features improved their matched control
sub: Both arms use 1,000 trees without early stopping. Timing added 44 positive snapshots: 235 to 279.
takeaway: The timing arm still trails the earlier early-stopped static control: 279 versus 289 captures. Tune them under one protocol next.
note: Paired lift difference +0.386; 95% interval [+0.098, +0.689]. Gain versus the stronger early-stopped baseline is untested.

title: The earlier experiments sharpened our approach
sub: Useful lessons from feature selection and model combinations.
rows: Original cohort, latest snapshot per patient: TRAIN-fold logistic AP 0.156 to about 0.19
Select inside training folds; do not assume the same gain for every model.
Keep strong tabular controls and test complementary captures.
Upstream feature processing used outcomes beyond TRAIN
Use fold-specific fitting and treat older results as exploratory.
Reuse its record; do not present it as a new experiment.
note: Historical results use different populations and metrics. They do not form a single comparable leaderboard.

title: Model stability is encouraging, but confirmation remains
sub: NLP fusion led the other Transformer variants across all three seeds.
takeaway: Selected-model train-to-validation lift gaps are 7â€“11%. Early stopping helps, but independent confirmation is still needed.
note: NLP versus static LightGBM: paired lift interval [+0.009, +0.802]. Validation influenced model selection.

title: The local pretraining pilot did not add value
sub: The matched scratch model outperformed local masked-code pretraining.
takeaway: 156 versus 198 positive snapshots captured. Both models were still improving at epoch 3; longer training remains untested.
note: Reported development run, same bounded TRAIN subset. Original pretrained Med-BERT weights were not used.

title: Pretrained biomedical text integration is ready to test
sub: The new implementation downloads pretrained Microsoft BiomedBERT and reuses the existing tensors.
items: Checkpoint download, weight checksums and local embedding inference passed. The biomedical text encoder stays frozen.
Count-only versus count plus random embeddings versus count plus pretrained medical-description embeddings.
Incremental predictive value on the full validation population. No new clinical lift or production improvement is claimed.
note: BiomedBERT is a biomedical text model, distinct from the original structured Med-BERT. Original Med-BERT weights are not publicly released.
